clue.text: A rogue — and others — can get money advanced

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little rogue
the rest means the others, everyone else

explanation.surface: A con man and his cronies manage to wangle a cash advance.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprest is a sum of money lent or advanced, originally to soldiers or officials for expenses.

clue.text: Force the changing of "Time's up"

indicators.note: changing the phrase means its letters are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: The end of the allotted time brings strong pressure for change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time's up' here supplies its S as a letter: it is 'time is up', not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is the driving force or momentum behind movement.

clue.text: Standard volume, but quite outstanding

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level, as in golf
a volume is a quantity or amount

explanation.surface: A normal amount, yet somehow exceptional.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme, above all others in importance.

clue.text: Uplifting Oriental tale giving delight

indicators.note: in a down entry, uplifting means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: An inspiring story from the East brings joy to its listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' turns ETALE (E plus TALE) to read upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate is to fill with joy or high spirits, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Two-nil score

explanation.surface: A football result of two goals to none.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-nil' looks like a match result, but written as figures, 2 and 0, it reads as the number; 'score' is the old word for that count.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-nil written in figures reads 20, and a score is an old counting unit of that many items.

clue.text: Pop round about unpleasant little protuberance

indicators.note: one word is wrapped round the other, enclosing it entirely

parts.note: pop and papa are both familiar words for a father
ill can mean unpleasant or harmful, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: Dad calls in about a nasty small swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A papilla is a small nipple-like bump on the body, such as on the tongue.

clue.text: Minister, a Labour leader of the country

parts.note: a pastor is a minister of a church

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A government minister described as one of Labour's rural leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks political alongside Labour but means a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral describes rural life and the countryside.

clue.text: With fences deals paid off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone bad or astray, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Property bargains settled for a fenced-in estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence of stakes, so something palisaded is enclosed by such fences.

clue.text: Superior European university

explanation.surface: A higher-ranking academic institution on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege lord is a feudal superior; Liège in Belgium is a city with a university.

clue.text: The manual worker having little heart is anxious

indicators.note: the clue words have a little piece of the answer within them, running across their boundaries

explanation.surface: A labourer with a timid heart frets.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled craftsperson who works with the hands.

clue.text: Carriage left to deteriorate

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
to age is to grow old and decline

explanation.surface: A coach abandoned to rot.
explanation.definitionFit: Portage is the carrying of boats or goods overland, or the charge for such conveyance.

clue.text: In a way strange and striking

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other word

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
alien means foreign or strange

explanation.surface: Something odd and remarkable about a certain manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A salient feature is prominent or conspicuous, catching the eye.

clue.text: One must use steps — may be tricky in stormy conditions

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters are rearranged in a puzzling way

explanation.surface: Advice to take care on stairs in bad weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempestuousness is the quality of being stormy or turbulent.

clue.text: Being short, top-drawer politician is in beastly accommodation

indicators.note: the first pieces go inside the housing word

parts.note: a sty houses pigs, a home for beasts
U means upper-class, top-drawer
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A small upper-class MP lives in a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumpy describes something short and thick, a squat build.

clue.text: It's a fruit, that's official

explanation.surface: A citrus that holds public office.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a small orange-like citrus, and also a senior bureaucrat or Chinese official.

clue.text: A rare drug administered for coping with back trouble

indicators.note: a drug administered is dealt out, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusual medicine prescribed for backache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back trouble' looks medical but means fighting at the rear of an army.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard protects an army's rear, dealing with attack from behind.

clue.text: Getting cash at this point, stick together

parts.note: a coin is a piece of cash
here means in this place or at this point

explanation.surface: Picking up money right here and staying united.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere or be united in one substance is the meaning, an uncommon synonym.

clue.text: Attending the big match or he'll swear!

parts.note: at means present at, attending
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A fan threatens to curse if they miss the big game.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: An attestor is one who testifies or bears witness formally.

clue.text: Men habitually sailing read a note and take flight

parts.note: ABs are able seamen
to con is to study or read over
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: Sailors read a message then flee.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to run away secretly, to flee.

clue.text: Single trade agreements -models of perfection

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, single
deals are trade agreements

explanation.surface: One-off trade pacts held up as exemplary.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are standards of perfection to aspire to.

clue.text: Place on a river producing furniture

parts.note: to set is to place
the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Setting up somewhere by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Settees are upholstered seats, pieces of sitting-room furniture.

clue.text: Some hundreds will be in a hole before Christmas!

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a vent is a hole for air
D is the Roman numeral 500, several hundreds

explanation.surface: Many hundreds will be in trouble before the holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a hole' looks like 'in trouble' but asks for D inside A VENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent is the church season leading up to Christmas.

clue.text: The outcome of having the bedroom window open at night?

definitions.text: The outcome of having the bedroom window open at night?

parts.words: The outcome of having the bedroom window open at night?
parts.note: a cold current of air blowing across someone in bed, read whimsically, rather than a sedative drink

explanation.surface: Wondering what a breezy night with the window open leads to.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeping draught is a drink that induces sleep, here read as a breeze over the sleeper.

clue.text: On rising doctors exercise here

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: MOs are medical officers, doctors
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: Getting up, medics do their workout in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the doctors above the exercise, and 'rising' turns the run upward; Epsom's Downs are where racehorses exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Racehorses are trained on Epsom Downs, the Surrey racecourse, so it is the place meant.

clue.text: A driver's cautious signal

parts.note: the traffic light between green and red warning a motorist to prepare to stop

explanation.surface: A careful motorist's indication.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is the middle traffic light colour, warning to stop.

clue.text: Keep taking notice

explanation.surface: Continue paying attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe a rule is to keep it; to observe is also to notice or watch.

clue.text: The all-round squeeze

parts.note: a pressing with the arms wrapped completely about someone, a hug

explanation.surface: A tight wrap-around pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: An embrace is a hug, a squeeze with arms all round.

clue.text: The estate seemed to be settled about the beginning of November

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the single letter
settled suggests the letters are rearranged into order
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Property appeared resolved early in November.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land held by a lord, an estate.

clue.text: Abuse one gets in some occupations

indicators.note: the single letter is placed within the other word

parts.note: trades are occupations
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Rudeness one encounters in certain jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirades are long angry speeches, verbal abuse.
